Content:
How do we write the following expression in words?

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5) - 6]

Content:
The order of operations can help! Since our expression uses parentheses, this operation comes first:

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5)]

Content:
So first, we say: "Multiply [MATH: 9] and [MATH: 5]".

Content:
The next operation is:

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5) \,\color{red}{-\, 6}]

Content:
So next, we say: "then subtract [MATH: 6]".

Content:
Combining our phrases, we get: "Multiply [MATH: 9] and [MATH: 5,] then subtract [MATH: 6.]"

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
How do we write the following expression in words?

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5) - 6]

Content:
The order of operations can help! Since our expression uses parentheses, this operation comes first:

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5)]

Content:
So first, we say: "Multiply [MATH: 9] and [MATH: 5]".

Content:
The next operation is:

Content:
[MATH: (9\times 5) \,\color{red}{-\, 6}]

Content:
So next, we say: "then subtract [MATH: 6]".

Content:
Combining our phrases, we get: "Multiply [MATH: 9] and [MATH: 5,] then subtract [MATH: 6.]"

Item 2 — Example: Writing an Expression in Words

Example Prompt:
What phrase represents the expression [MATH: (9 - 7) \times 2?]

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since the expression uses parentheses, this operation comes first. So first, we should "Subtract [MATH: 7] from [MATH: 9]".

The [MATH: \times\,2] means that we should "then multiply by [MATH: 2]".

So, the given expression is equivalent to "Subtract [MATH: 7] from [MATH: 9], then multiply by [MATH: 2.]"
